chunks: Everything in this book that is narrated from Abd Al-Mu'min ibn Al-Qasim Al-Ansari Al-Kufi has been transmitted by me from my father - may Allah have mercy on him - from Sad ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn ibn Abi Al-Khattab, from Al-Hakam ibn Maskeen, from Abu Kahmas, from Abd Al-Mu'min ibn Al-Qasim Al-Ansari Al-Kufi
who was an Arab, and he is the brother of Abu Maryam Abd Al-Ghaffar ibn Al-Qasim Al-Ansari

key_terms.أبو مريم: Abu Maryam, the brother of the main narrator
key_terms.سعد بن عبد الله: Sad ibn Abdullah, a key narrator in the chain
key_terms.عبد المؤمن بن القاسم الأنصاري الكوفي: Abd Al-Mu'min ibn Al-Qasim Al-Ansari Al-Kufi, a specific narrator
key_terms.محمد بن الحسين: Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, a narrator in the chain

ai.seo_question: Who is Abd Al-Mu'min ibn Al-Qasim Al-Ansari and what is his transmission chain in Shia hadith literature?
ai.summary: This passage from *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih* provides a critical biographical verification (isnad) for Abd Al-Mu'min ibn Al-Qasim, a key narrator in Shaykh al-Saduq's collection. By explicitly tracing the chain through prominent figures like Al-Hakam ibn Miskin and identifying Abd Al-Mu'min as an Arab and brother of Abu Maryam, al-Saduq reinforces the reliability and tribal authenticity of the transmission, a common scholarly practice to establish trustworthiness in hadith sciences.
